### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
delta-kernel-rs and chdig are built as members of the Rust workspace in `contrib/rust-contrib-workspace`, with one `Cargo.lock`, one cargo target directory and features resolved once for all members, so the crates they share with the other Rust libraries are compiled once, in one parallel cargo run.

### Description

Step 3 of the layout in #86562, after #130348 (step 2).

- `contrib/delta-kernel-rs-cmake` and `contrib/chdig-cmake` get one-line wrapper crates (`pub use delta_kernel_ffi;`, `pub use chdig;`), imported through the workspace manifest like the other six.
- One environment for every member (`clickhouse_config_crate_env`: OpenSSL variables, `CFLAGS` with `-I contrib/openssl/include`, `CARGO_HOME`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`): build scripts track their environment, so any difference rebuilds shared crates every build.
- `resolver.feature-unification = "workspace"`: corrosion runs one `cargo rustc` per package, and cargo otherwise resolves features per package.
- The workspace manifest is also a root package, `_ch_rust_workspace`, with one feature per member. `contrib/rust-contrib-workspace/CMakeLists.txt` builds it with the enabled members' features before their runs, which then compile only their wrapper. Not with LTO, where each member's run does its own code generation. The wrappers are plain libraries imported with `OVERRIDE_CRATE_TYPE <crate>=staticlib`, so the root run writes no unused archives.
- `Cargo.lock` is resolved offline from `contrib/rust_vendor` (no `rust_vendor` change); delta-kernel-rs and chdig take the workspace's semver-compatible versions.
- The `aws-lc-sys` `LDFLAGS` workaround goes: the crate left the graph.
- `contrib/delta-kernel-rs` moves to the merge commit of ClickHouse/delta-kernel-rs#22: the pin of #130062 plus `crate-type = ["lib"]`.

Rust-only cold build, `-j48`: Debug 200 s / 1027 s CPU on master, 108 s / 779 s here. With ThinLTO 13.2 min on master, 18.4 min here: the members' LTO runs queue on the one target directory.

Validation, x86_64 Debug:
- 1240 compile units in 3 target directories before, 799 in one after, no crate built with two feature sets.
- Build and link pass; a no-op build compiles nothing, also alternating between members; the member archives are the same cargo units as without the root package.
- Delta Lake stateless tests 77/77; prql, pco, polyglot, vortex and wasm tests 98/99 (the other fails on master too); `chdig --help` works.

comment.body:
@groeneai The 37% longer wall time you report is recoverable within this PR, or in step 4 right after it. I prototyped it on top of this layout:

- Make the workspace manifest a root package, `_ch_rust_workspace`, with `crate-type = ["staticlib"]`, one feature per member (`prql = ["dep:_ch_rust_prql"]`, ...) and the members as optional path dependencies; `src/lib.rs` re-exports each behind its `#[cfg(feature)]`.
- Give the wrapper crates `crate-type = ["staticlib", "lib"]`, so that the root package can depend on them. The per-crate `cargo rustc --crate-type=staticlib` runs are unaffected.
- Add `contrib/rust-contrib-workspace/CMakeLists.txt`, added last in `contrib/CMakeLists.txt`: it collects the enabled `_ch_rust_*` targets, imports the root package through `RUST_CONTRIB_WORKSPACE_MANIFEST` with `CRATES _ch_rust_workspace FEATURES <enabled>`, applies the same env function as the members (without `corrosion_link_libraries` and the localize step), and for every member does `add_dependencies(cargo-prebuild_<member> cargo-build__ch_rust_workspace)` plus copies the member's `_cargo-build_` `MANUALLY_ADDED_DEPENDENCIES` (`cxx`, OpenSSL) onto `_cargo-build__ch_rust_workspace`, skipping the `cargo-prebuild_*` ones to avoid a cycle.

Going through Corrosion for that run, rather than a hand-written `cargo build`, is what makes the environment and flags identical to the members' runs; with the feature unification you already have, the members' runs then compile exactly one unit each, the wrapper. For that to hold, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` has to move into the common environment too (the delta-kernel build script writes its header there; the per-crate run and the root run must agree), so set it for all crates, not only for `_ch_rust_delta_kernel`.

Release, x86_64, no compiler cache, 32 cores, clean target directory, cargo targets only: the six crates of #130348 take 180 s (serialized on the lock), chdig and delta-kernel 51 s and 36 s in their own directories; with the root package all eight take 115 s, of which the root run is 104 s and the eight per-crate runs 3 to 5 s each. The cost is the unused archive of the root package, about 600 MiB in Release.

Two small things in the current diff: the `LDFLAGS` line can stay removed, `aws-lc-sys` is indeed gone from the lock; and resolving the lock offline against the existing vendor, as you did, is the right call, it avoids a `rust_vendor` PR entirely.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Pull request with some product improvements

issue.body:
**Allow batch `DeleteObjects` to use SHA256 digests, so batch delete becomes possible on FIPS-mode builds.**

This PR adds the `delete_checksum_algorithm` request setting. Options are `MD5`, `CRC32`, `SHA256`, configured via disk config and named collections, no query-level setting. `DeleteObjectsRequest` now sends a flexible checksum when an algorithm is set and `Content-MD5` otherwise.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Code was LLM-assisted. PR body skeleton started out that way, but I've heavily revised it.

**Why this is needed**

`DeleteObjects` requires `Content-MD5` or an `x-amz-checksum-*` header. `DeleteObjectsRequest` always took the legacy `Content-MD5` path on ordinary buckets. Under FIPS (`-DUSE_OPENSSL_FIPS=1` and a FIPS enabled OpenSSL config) the AWS SDK cannot compute MD5 and silently omits the header. This is seen in the broken `DeleteObjects` on Minio in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/125502 but can also be observed on AWS where ClickHouse quietly falls back to slower, more expensive individual `DeleteObject` calls. 

Without an explicit value `DeleteObjects` uses `Content-MD5`, or `SHA256` when the `MD5` digest cannot be fetched
(`OpenSSLInitializer::isMD5Available`). A server that rejects `Content-MD5` gets one retry of the batch with `SHA256`, which is remembered in `S3Capabilities` for later batches; if that is also rejected, the existing fallback to `DeleteObject` applies. An explicit value for the config option is never overridden by fallback. An explicit `MD5` is an error when it cannot work (under FIPS, `S3Express`). `S3Express` defaults to `CRC32`. `GCS` keeps `Content-MD5`; `delete_checksum_algorithm` does not apply to it. Discovery decisions are logged.

**Implementation choices**

I didn't re-use `upload_checksum_algorithm`'s value because S3-compatible endpoints can differ in their requirements and support for checksums on upload vs batch delete. It's entirely possible that there could be working deployments that have SHSA256 for upload and MD5 for delete, where upgrading delete to SH256 would break delete. Hence the new setting.

Currently the new `delete_checksum_algorithm` setting doesn't have a session-setting counterpart like `s3_upload_checksum_algorithm` has for `upload_checksum_algorithm`.  I'm not really sure why the session-setting was added for upload, but adding a delete equivalent probably doesn't make sense. Upload requests are (often) constructed during the user's session (e.g. for direct s3 table function or engine, backup to S3); most deletes are background/asynchronous where a session setting wouldn't apply anyway.

I've updated `upload_checksum_algorithm`'s check to switch from `isFIPSEnabled` to the new `isMD5Available()` so it really checks MD5, not just FIPS. Happy to drop that and make the delete check also use the existing `isMD5Available` if you prefer, but I thought it preferable to check the actual capability directly.

~~If you want to actually test a FIPS mode build ( `-DOPENSSL_USE_FIPS=1`) you will need to merge https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/125548 first, either into master or into a dev branch that combines with this one. Otherwise a pre-existing bug will cause a linker error.~~ Update: Merged, master is now buildable with `-DOPENSSL_USE_FIPS=1`.

**Docs**

Updates docs to document the existing `upload_checksum_algorithm` and new `delete_checksum_algorithm`. Previously the only docs cover for `upload_checksum_algorithm` was for its session setting `s3_upload_checksum_algorithm`.

**Testing**

I've built a container image [`ghcr.io/ringerc/clickhouse-patches:fips-test-b6641b2f620`](https://github.com/ringerc/ClickHouse-patches/pkgs/container/clickhouse-patches/1376705776?tag=fips-test-b6641b2f620) off the tag [issue-125521-and-125548](https://github.com/ringerc/ClickHouse-patches/releases/tag/issue-125521-and-125548) that combines this PR branch and the branch in #125548 (to fix FIPS builds) that you can use to test this build out. issue.title: Static PIE RELRO, aarch64 LSE atomics, thread and condvar fixes for the static binary
issue.body:
Brings the musl changes that the statically linked ClickHouse binary (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109239) pins into `ClickHouse/v1.2.6`. `aarch64-lse-futex` is that PR's musl line. It has already merged `ClickHouse/v1.2.6`, including #8 and #9, so this merges cleanly.

- Make `PT_GNU_RELRO` read-only in a static PIE. `rcrt1.o` never ran the dynamic linker's RELRO `mprotect`, so the GOT stayed writable.
- Use LSE atomics on aarch64 when the target has them.
- Size the stack of new threads from `RLIMIT_STACK`, like glibc, and give them the same stack alignment as glibc.
- Spin briefly in `pthread_cond_timedwait` before sleeping on the futex.
- Two fixes for normal mutexes waited on through a condvar: keep the lock word in the contended state, and never take the uncontended fast path in a signaled waiter.
- Unwind info for the x86_64 `__clone` (end of stack) and `__restore_rt` (sigframe).
- Size the rseq registration by the extensible rseq ABI.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109239

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Merged together they give exactly the tree of `aarch64-lse-futex`; that branch stays, because https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109239 pins its commit `bc7dd5bd`.

The `GROUP BY` top-K optimization (`enable_group_by_top_k_optimization`) now also applies when a matched `GROUP BY` key is sorted with `COLLATE`, e.g. `GROUP BY s ORDER BY s COLLATE 'en' LIMIT 10`.

### Description

The optimization was disabled for a `COLLATE` on a matched key. Now `TopKParams` owns the collators, the heap compares collated keys with `compareAtWithCollation` and keeps keys tied with the boundary, and `Aggregating` step v2 serializes each key's locale (plan version 22; older peers get no collated top-K). A collated first key gets no dynamic filter, whose per-row locale comparison would continue after the heap freezes.

A locale comparison costs more than a hash lookup, so with a collated heap the aggregation loops look a row's key up first: a known key is aggregated without a comparison, and only a new key is compared with the boundary. The serialized method of a composite key still compares first, because its key holder is costly to build twice. Otherwise a collated heap starts and freezes like any other.

| Query | off | on |
|---|---|---|
| `URL` | 895 ms | 382 ms |
| `URL`, 1 thread | 7312 ms | 5729 ms |
| `URL, b` (serialized method) | 1229 ms | 366 ms |
| 20M unique `toString(number)` | 96 ms | 24 ms |
| 1M keys in descending cycles | 67 ms | 35 ms |
| 300K keys in cycles | 66 ms | 35 ms |

CI runs the `URL`, unique and descending-cycles cases in `topk_aggregation_collate.xml`; `05407_group_by_top_k_collation` checks every case against off, also with `sum`, `uniqExact` and no aggregate functions.

### Description

On 26.10.3.7 (also 26.8 and 26.3), `SELECT license_path FROM system.licenses WHERE library_name = 'libxml2'` returns `/contrib/libxml2/test/html-tokenizer/NOTICE`, the notice of an html5lib test fixture, instead of `/contrib/libxml2/Copyright`. `rapidjson` shows `contrib/natvis/LICENSE` (a debugger visualizer, the file behind the warning fixed in #99909), `sz3` shows `tools/pysz/LICENSE`, and `pdqsort` has no row although it is compiled in.

The builder image (Ubuntu 24.04) has mawk, where `/LICENSE/`, `/COPY/` and `/NOTICE/` are case-sensitive, so a lowercase top-level `license.txt` or `Copyright` is never chosen: a deeper upper-case file wins, or nothing matches. The program now upper-cases the file name with `toupper` and matches on the basename only, which is POSIX awk. Matching the basename also fixes GNU awk on a checkout path containing "license", where every candidate matched and configure failed with `sources with unknown license found in aws-c-s3`.

Validation: the script output is byte-identical under gawk, mawk, busybox awk and `gawk --posix`, for a plain path and a path containing "license", and equals today's gawk output, so gawk builds do not change; official builds gain the `pdqsort` row and 3 corrected rows (`rapidjson` becomes `BSD`, as in gawk builds). `01276_system_licenses` gains the `libxml2` and `pdqsort` rows (`rapidjson` and `sz3` are not checked out in Fast test): 50/50 OK on a mawk-configured build, FAIL on the CI master binary of the same commit.

issue.title: [libc] Avoid mask round trip through the stack in AVX-512 bcmp
issue.body:
`neq<__m512i>` folds the 64-bit `vpcmpneqb` mask into 32 bits by OR-ing its two halves. InstCombine turns that into two `extractelement`s of `bitcast <64 x i1> to <2 x i32>`. VectorCombine (`foldExtractExtract`) then rewrites them as a `<2 x i32>` shuffle + `or`. X86 can only lower that bitcast by spilling the mask register and reloading it into an xmm register. The 16-byte reload overlaps the 8-byte store, so it can't be store-forwarded, and every 64-byte block of the bcmp loop pays a store-forwarding stall.

```asm
; before (per 64 B block)
vpcmpneqb  %zmm1, %zmm0, %k0
kmovq      %k0, -8(%rsp)
vmovdqa    -8(%rsp), %xmm0      ; store-forwarding stall
vpshufd    $85, %xmm0, %xmm1
vpor       %xmm0, %xmm1, %xmm0
vmovd      %xmm0, %eax

; after
vpcmpneqd  (%rsi,%rax,1), %zmm0, %k0
kortestw   %k0, %k0
```

All callers (`Bcmp::block`/`tail`/`head_tail`/`loop_and_tail_offset`) only test the result for non-zero, so return `mask != 0`. This matches what `neq<__m128i>` and `neq<__m256i>` already do. Because only "any difference" is observable now, LLVM also narrows the byte compare to a dword compare, whose 16-bit mask can be tested directly with `kortestw`.

Results with `-march=x86-64-v4`, clang 23.1.1, AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D (Zen 5), ns/call:

| size | x86-64-v3 | x86-64-v4 (before) | x86-64-v4 (after) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512 B | 4.09 | 34.40 | 3.14 |
| 4 KiB | 26.75 | 270.33 | 18.04 |
| 16 KiB | 114.49 | 1078.29 | 80.91 |

Before this change the AVX-512 build was 5–15x slower than the AVX2 build for every size above 64 B. memcmp is unaffected. Also reproduces with clang 21.1.8.

issue.title: `addDays`/`addWeeks`/`subtractDays` on UTC `DateTime64`: 14% slower on aarch64

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Date/DateTime/TimeZone datatypes and date-time semantics.

issue.body:
### Describe what's wrong

- On aarch64, `addDays`, `addWeeks` and `subtractDays` over a `DateTime64the statement belowsubtractWeeks` got ~10% faster.
- Results are unchanged.
- Local A/B on Neoverse-V2, master `6d8c8e92` (merge parent) vs `241ddc97` (#127213's merge commit), `max_threads=1`, pinned core, 30 runs each: `addDays` 0.440 -> 0.502 s, `addWeeks` 0.438 -> 0.502 s, `subtractDays` 0.444 -> 0.502 s, `subtractWeeks` 0.560 -> 0.502 s; controls (`DateTime` `addDays`, no-function baseline) unchanged.
- Distributions do not overlap.
- CI `Performance Comparison (arm_release)` on #127213: `add_days_fixed_offsetthe statement belowslower` in the last run); the same query sits at ~1.00 across ~300 other PR runs of 2026-10-30/31.
- PR #109239, which carries the same two-file change, went from 1.00 to 1.14 on #4/#5 when it picked #127213 up.

```
column in a fixed-offset time zone (UTC) got ~14% slower per query after #127213 (where this was found; not confirmed as the cause); the function's own per-row cost grew ~75% (0.084 s -> 0.146 s over 50M rows after subtracting the input-generation baseline).
#4/#5/#6 at 1.13-1.15 in all 5 runs over 3 commits (#5 flagged
```

Root cause: After #127213 (where this was found; not confirmed as the cause) the aarch64 loop in `Processor<AddDaysImpl, true>::vectorConstant<DataTypeDateTime64>` is no longer versioned on loop invariants. The back-edge targets the `exp10_i64(scale)` bounds check, so every row redoes the table load for `scaleMultiplier(scale)` (:379) and all multiplier-dependent products in `dayShiftStaysWithinLUT` (`seconds_per_day_scaled`, `lut_min_scaled`, the `DATE_LUT_SIZE` and `days` overflow checks): 48 instructions with 4 `mul` + 2 `smulh` + `madd` on the fast path. Before #127213 the compiler emitted four loop copies keyed on `scale <= 18` and the delta-overflow test; the fast path was 29 instructions with 1 `mul` + 1 `madd`. `subtractWeeks` was the one transform left out of line before (a per-row call to `SubtractIntervalImpl<AddWeeksImpl>::executeWithOffsetMode<true>`), which is why only it improved.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `FunctionDateOrDateTimeAddInterval::executeImpl` -> `DateTimeAddIntervalImpl::execute` (`hasFixedOffset` -> `executeWithOffsetMode<true>`, FunctionDateOrDateTimeAddInterval.h:965-968) -> `Processor<Transform, true>::vectorConstant` loop (:829-831) -> `executeTransform`, now `ALWAYS_INLINE` with a statement-level `[[clang::always_inline]]` (:865-870) -> `AddDaysImpl::executeWithOffsetMode<true>(DateTime64)` (:376-386) -> `DateLUTImpl::dayShiftStaysWithinLUT` (DateLUTImpl.h:542).

Affected locations:
- [`src/Functions/FunctionDateOrDateTimeAddInterval.h:870`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5db76d79a71e39/src/Functions/FunctionDateOrDateTimeAddInterval.h#L870) — forced inline of `executeWithOffsetMode<fixed_offset>` into the per-row loops
- [`src/Functions/FunctionDateOrDateTimeAddInterval.h:379`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5db76d79a71e39/src/Functions/FunctionDateOrDateTimeAddInterval.h#L379) — `AddDaysImpl` `DateTime64` fast path: `scaleMultiplier(scale)` + `dayShiftStaysWithinLUT` now recomputed per row
- [`src/Functions/FunctionDateOrDateTimeAddInterval.h:476`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5db76d79a71e39/src/Functions/FunctionDateOrDateTimeAddInterval.h#L476) — `AddWeeksImpl` `DateTime64` fast path, same shape
- [`src/Common/DateLUTImpl.h:542`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/5db76d79a71e39/src/Common/DateLUTImpl.h#L542) — `dayShiftStaysWithinLUT`: loop-invariant products no longer hoisted

Impact: ARM servers running `addDays`/`addWeeks`/`subtractDays` over `DateTime64` in UTC or any fixed-offset zone pay ~75% more CPU inside the function, ~14% on a query dominated by it (the existing `add_days_fixed_offset` perf test). Correct results; master only (merged 2026-10-31, not in a release).

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Likely yes — see additional context.

### How to reproduce

B=https://clickhouse-builds.s3.amazonaws.com/REFs/master
curl -sSo pre  $B/6d8c8e92041c37d7a4f04134dfd44fd5dd4aed2c/masterci/build_arm_release/clickhouse
curl -sSo post $B/241ddc97c2b229b94d1725abc14e48be599fda84/masterci/build_arm_release/clickhouse
chmod +x pre post
for f in addDays addWeeks subtractDays subtractWeeks; do Q="SELECT sum(toUInt32($f(t, 7))) FROM (SELECT toDateTime64(1600000000.123 + number % 50000000, 3, 'UTC') AS t FROM numbers(50000000)) FORMAT Null"; for b in pre post; do echo "$f $b"; taskset -c 2 ./$b local --path /tmp/ch_$b --max_threads=1 --time --query "$Q; $Q; $Q; $Q; $Q"; done; done
llvm-objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn --start-address=0x126b0b00 --stop-address=0x126b0f1c pre
llvm-objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn --start-address=0x126b0440 --stop-address=0x126b06b8 post

### Expected behavior

```
Pre-PR medians: q4_addDays 0.440 s, q5_addWeeks 0.438 s, q6_subDays 0.444 s (post-PR should stay within noise, as the base64 and DateTime controls do).
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

```
query              n  pre_med post_med  pre_max post_min  ratio
base64            30    0.356    0.356    0.686    0.352  1.000
q4_addDays        30    0.440    0.502    0.442    0.498  1.141
q5_addWeeks       30    0.438    0.502    0.440    0.498  1.146
q6_subDays        30    0.444    0.502    0.472    0.498  1.131
q7_subWeeks       30    0.560    0.502    0.587    0.499  0.896
q0_dt_addDays   
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Make the invariants explicit instead of relying on loop unswitching: compute `multiplier` and the `dayShiftStaysWithinLUT` bounds (`lut_min_scaled`, `lut_end_guard`, `days * seconds_per_day_scaled`) once per column in `Processor::vectorConstant` and hand them to the fixed-offset transform, so the per-row fast path is two compares and an add. Trade-off: just dropping the forced inline on the `supports_fixed_offset_dispatch` branch would bring back the per-row out-of-line call `subtractWeeks` had before (0.560 s vs 0.502 s here).

</details>

### Additional context

Open risks:
- x86-64, CI only: `add_days_lut_range_check #8` (`addDays(DateTime64, 1, 'Asia/Istanbul')`, the query #127213 (where this was found; not confirmed as the cause) targets) is at 1.050-1.062 on amd_release in all 5 runs, vs p10-p90 0.99-1.012 for other PRs since 2026-10-24; on arm it is 0.93 (faster). Not reproduced locally.
- `vectorVector`/`constantVector` and the `Time64` instantiations go through the same `executeTransform`; not measured.

Found during automated review of [PR #127213](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127213); this finding was not executed, so nobody is tagged. The cited lines predate that PR: per git blame they were introduced by #109836 (Arithmetic fast path for addDays/addWeeks in fixed-offset time zones) and #118501. Severity P3 · Finding `h_pr127213_001`

issue.title: Vectorized memchr and strlen for x86_64 in libllvmlibc

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Pull request with some performance improvements

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Third-party deps updates in contrib/, vendored code, and platform base libraries.

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: At least one submodule changed in this PR.

issue.body:
Split from https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109239, kept separate so a perf regression can be reverted alone.

musl ships x86_64 assembly only for `memcpy`, `memmove` and `memset`; its `memchr` and `strlen` are generic word-at-a-time C, and LLVM-libc's are byte and word loops. In the performance comparison of the musl binary the CSV parser spent 11.4% of its samples in `memchr` against 5.1% in glibc's `__memchr_evex`. This adds strong `memchr` and `strlen` to `libllvmlibc`, which is linked `--whole-archive` ahead of musl.

One body, two tiers from one TU: the build's baseline (AVX2 at x86-64-v3, SSE2 in the compat build) and an AVX-512BW clone with 64-byte vectors and mask registers, selected once at runtime through a function pointer, the same shape as `x86_64_mem_functions.cpp`. The 64-byte tier is what matches glibc above 4 KiB; 32-byte vectors cap at 1.6x its time because of load width. The head, three straight-line vectors, a 4-vector loop aligned to its own stride and a masked tail follow glibc's `memchr-evex`. Aligned loads never cross a page, `memchr` tracks the remaining byte count rather than `s + n`, so an `n` that overstates the object (musl's `strnlen` forwards the caller's limit, `realpath` passes `PATH_MAX`, `SIZE_MAX` is legal) still stops at the first match without touching the next page.

**Sanitizers.** ASan, MSan and TSan intercept `memchr` and `strlen` by defining those symbols themselves: the interceptor checks the range from `s` to the result, then forwards to the real libc function. This implementation cannot run as instrumented code at all, for the same reason glibc's assembly cannot: it deliberately reads whole aligned vectors past `n` and past the match, inside the page, which instrumented loads would report as an overflow and MSan as a branch on uninitialized bytes. So in sanitizer builds the interceptor must win the link and the file is not compiled there (the same arrangement as `memmem.cpp`); the interceptor then forwards to musl's `memchr`/`strlen`, which is what sanitizer CI exercises today. Nothing is bypassed: sanitizer builds get the checks plus musl, release builds get this code. Pointing the interceptor's real-function slot at this code (compiled `no_sanitize`) so that sanitizer CI also covers it is possible with the static-link interception machinery of #109239 and is left for that PR.

Measured with a libc microbenchmark harness (every implementation renamed and linked into one binary, called through function pointers, pinned) on Zen 5 (glibc 2.44 = `__memchr_evex512`), ns per call, aligned:

| | 64 B | 256 B | 1 KiB | 4 KiB | 1 MiB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `memchr` musl | 5.0 | 12.3 | 53 | 186 | 43499 |
| `memchr` glibc | 1.49 | 1.70 | 3.5 | 11.8 | 3866 |
| `memchr` this PR, v3 build | 1.69 | 2.16 | 3.8 | 9.7 | 3832 |
| `memchr` this PR, AVX2 tier only | 1.51 | 2.83 | 4.0 | 13.1 | 6306 |
| `strlen` musl | 2.9 | 9.1 | 34 | 139 | 33802 |
| `strlen` glibc | 1.13 | 1.69 | 2.9 | 8.6 | 3730 |
| `strlen` this PR, v3 build | 1.50 | 2.00 | 3.2 | 9.0 | 3850 |

On random sizes up to 4 KiB with no match the PR is at 14.4 ns against glibc's 13.4 ns and musl's 103 ns.

The unit test runs the buffer between two `PROT_NONE` pages at every misalignment and covers the ISO C contract plus the properties callers rely on: a limit that overstates the object by one byte, one vector, pages or up to `SIZE_MAX` with the match anywhere in the buffer, the first of several matches, conversion of `c` to `unsigned char`, bytes that differ from `c` in one bit or the sign bit around the match, strings of high bytes with garbage after the terminator, and a 32 MiB buffer. It passes against glibc and against this code with the AVX-512 clone, the AVX2 tier and the SSE2 tier.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109239

- Performance Improvement

Add vectorized `memchr` and `strlen` implementations for x86_64 with runtime AVX-512 dispatch.

- CVE-2026-119375: uninitialized page-cache read from a WAL file with an undersized page.

- `ClickHouse/3.54.1` is the official 3.54.1 amalgamation plus the two ClickHouse TSan patches (`_Atomic int isInit`, `_Atomic pid_t randomnessPid`), ClickHouse/sqlite-amalgamation#4 and #5.
